fieldMarks: Underparts mostly spotted rather than barred
In flight shows a longer tail with white outer feathers
Sexes similar; male slightly larger (38–53 cm)
behavior: Displays on leks; seasonal home ranges are usually within about 2 km of the lek
May roost at night by burrowing into snowdrifts
Forages on the ground in summer and in trees and shrubs in winter, when it eats buds; takes grasshoppers and other insects in summer
habitat: Open prairie mixed with groves of aspen, birch, willow or shrubs, forest edges and open burns in coniferous forest; more open grassland in summer, groves in winter.
range: Resident locally from Alaska and Yukon east to western Quebec and south to eastern Washington, Idaho, Utah, Colorado, Nebraska, the Dakotas, Minnesota, Wisconsin and northern Michigan; it has disappeared from parts of its former southern range.

lookalikes.name: Greater and lesser prairie-chickens
lookalikes.howToTell: Prairie-chickens have barred underparts; the sharp-tail is spotted and has a longer, white-edged tail.
